codes.meaning: Low pressure drop or refrigerant shortage
repairSteps: Inspect for refrigerant leaks at all connections
Verify outdoor unit fan is running
Check for blockage in refrigerant circuit

codes.meaning: Power supply insufficient or voltage drop
repairSteps: Measure supply voltage at indoor and outdoor unit terminals
Check main breaker and wiring connections
Verify wire gauge is adequate for cable run length

codes.meaning: Communication error between indoor and outdoor units
repairSteps: Check wiring connections between indoor and outdoor units
Verify power supply to outdoor unit
Reset the system by turning off power for 30 seconds
If persists, check the PCB for damage

codes.meaning: Communication error between indoor units in multi-system or with remote controller
repairSteps: Check for interference from other electrical equipment

codes.meaning: Safety device activated on outdoor unit
repairSteps: Check all safety devices on outdoor unit
Check for short circuits in wiring
Measure insulation resistance of compressor windings
Check high-pressure switch and low-pressure switch

codes.meaning: Outdoor unit PCB defective
repairSteps: Check power supply to outdoor PCB
Inspect PCB for visible damage or burnt components
Check all connectors on PCB are secure
Measure voltages at PCB test points

codes.meaning: High pressure switch activated
repairSteps: Check outdoor unit airflow and clean condenser coil
Inspect for non-condensable gases in system
Check high pressure switch wiring and operation

codes.meaning: Compressor motor overload or overcurrent protection activated
Compressor motor lock or stall detected
repairSteps: Check compressor winding resistance (phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground)
Replace compressor if windings are shorted

codes.meaning: Outdoor fan motor lock or stall detected
repairSteps: Check for obstructions around outdoor fan
Verify fan motor connector on PCB

codes.meaning: Electronic expansion valve malfunction
repairSteps: Inspect valve for debris or ice blockage
Replace expansion valve if coil is open/short

codes.meaning: Discharge pipe temperature too high
Refrigerant system high pressure abnormality
repairSteps: Check condenser coil for dirt or blockage

codes.meaning: Indoor unit position detection sensor error
repairSteps: Check position detection switch or sensor

codes.meaning: DC fan compressor current sensor error
repairSteps: Check current sensor on outdoor PCB
Replace current sensor or PCB if faulty

codes.meaning: Outdoor air temperature thermistor error
repairSteps: Measure thermistor resistance and compare to temperature chart
Replace thermistor if resistance is out of range

codes.meaning: Discharge pipe thermistor malfunction
repairSteps: Verify thermistor is properly attached to discharge pipe
Replace thermistor if out of range

codes.meaning: Heat exchanger thermistor malfunction on outdoor unit
repairSteps: Measure thermistor resistance at current temperature
Check wiring from thermistor to PCB
Verify thermistor is clipped to heat exchanger properly
Replace thermistor if readings are incorrect

codes.meaning: Inverter compressor heat sink temperature too high
repairSteps: Verify outdoor fan is operating at correct speed
Inspect for ambient temperature above rated maximum

codes.meaning: Compressor overcurrent at startup or during operation
repairSteps: Verify supply voltage is within specification
Check for liquid refrigerant in compressor crankcase
Inspect IPM (Intelligent Power Module) on outdoor PCB
